questions.question: What actually separates programmatic SEO done well from done badly?
questions.answer_summary: The dividing line is genuine per-page value versus templated pages that just swap in a keyword/location/product name with no unique substance.

questions.question: Does Google actually ban programmatic SEO as a technique?
questions.answer_summary: No — Google's spam policies don't name 'programmatic SEO'; what's banned is 'scaled content abuse,' an intent-based policy that can apply to any mass-page-production method, automated or not.

questions.question: What is a doorway page and how does it relate to programmatic SEO penalties?
questions.answer_summary: A doorway page is created purely to rank for a query and funnel visitors elsewhere; a cited example was 5,000 'plumber in [city]' pages that all redirected to one contact form.

questions.question: What happened when a site scaled programmatic pages badly?
questions.answer_summary: A law firm site that generated roughly 42,000 near-identical city pages (same body text, swapped city/name) reportedly suffered a 96% traffic drop.

questions.question: What does programmatic SEO done well look like at scale?
questions.answer_summary: Zapier is repeatedly cited as the reference example: 50,000+ integration pages driving roughly 5.8M monthly organic visits.

questions.question: How much AI-assisted publishing volume starts to look automated/spammy to Google?
questions.answer_summary: Sustained publishing of 10+ articles per day for months is flagged as a red flag, since human editorial teams typically produce at most 10-15 quality pieces per week.

questions.question: Is there a 'safe' productivity multiplier when using AI to help scale content?
questions.answer_summary: A 2-4x productivity boost over a human baseline is described as sustainable, whereas 40-100x increases are a warning sign of scaled abuse.

questions.question: How much traffic can a scaled-content-abuse penalty cost, by site type?
questions.answer_summary: Reported ranges include roughly 60-80% for niche info sites with 500+ AI pages, 40-70% for affiliate review sites, and 30-60% for location-based service pages.

questions.question: Should programmatic pages be launched all at once or ramped up gradually?
questions.answer_summary: Practitioners recommend ramping gradually (e.g., roughly 1-3 posts/day scaling to 11-19/day) rather than dumping hundreds of pages at once, to avoid triggering a 'sudden programmatic content' signal that can get a site sandboxed.

questions.question: Can newly launched programmatic pages get indexed reliably?
questions.answer_summary: One 2026 case study reported 283 of roughly 400 pages indexed, with only about 2% stuck in 'Crawled - Currently Not Indexed' — described by the builder as a strong result for programmatic content.

questions.question: Is duplicate/templated structure risky even without obvious keyword stuffing?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — 'data-template pages' that swap only location, product, or keyword variants into an otherwise identical structure are explicitly called out as a scaled-abuse pattern.

questions.question: What's the actual success factor behind programmatic SEO that works?
questions.answer_summary: Practitioners frame it as: the goal isn't creating 100,000 pages, it's providing real value on those 100,000 pages — original insight or data per page rather than volume alone.

questions.question: Which industries have used programmatic SEO successfully beyond SaaS?
questions.answer_summary: Travel, real estate, and ecommerce platforms, along with sites like eBay, are cited as successful programmatic SEO verticals alongside Zapier.
